lines: On February 28, 1919, a man came to Dr. Schofield's house.
Man: Dr. Schofield, ⓐ<u>I have a special favor asking you</u>.
Dr. Schofield: What can I do for you?
Man: ⓑ<u>Many people are going to gathering tomorrow</u> for the independence of Korea. Could you take pictures __(B)__ the event and ⓒ<u>share it with the world</u>?
At 2 p.m. on March 1, ⓓ<u>Dr. Schofield was hiding in a building and saw a large group of people gathering outside</u>. __(A)__, he began to take pictures.
Dr. Schofield: Unbelievable! ⓔ<u>There is so many people here.</u> I hope the world will learn about this important event through my pictures.

items.stem: 윗글의 흐름상 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 수 없는 것은?
choices: Then
Soon
However
After that
Right away
items.explain: 사람들이 모이는 것을 본 뒤 곧바로 사진을 찍기 시작한 흐름. 역접 However는 맞지 않는다. 원문은 ‘He began to take pictures.’ 앞에 연결어를 넣어 물었다.

items.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 옳은 것은?
items.explain: ⓐ favor를 꾸미는 to부정사: asking → to ask / ⓑ be going to + 동사원형: gathering → gather / ⓒ pictures를 받으므로 it → them / ⓔ There are so many people. ⓓ 지각동사 saw + 목적어 + 현재분사(gathering)로 옳다.
items.source: L6 본문 1~2문단 · 통합본 L6 GRAMMAR 지각동사

items.stem: 윗글의 흐름상 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 단어로 알맞은 것은?
choices: of
to
for
at
with
items.explain: take a picture of: ~의 사진을 찍다.
items.source: L6 본문 1문단 · L6 어휘 take a picture of

items.stem: 윗글을 읽고 대답을 찾을 수 없는 질문은?
choices: On February 28, 1919, who came to Dr. Schofield's house?
Was Dr. Schofield asked to take pictures of an important event?
On March 1, where was Dr. Schofield hiding?
How many pictures did Dr. Schofield take?
Did Dr. Schofield hope the world would learn about the event?
items.explain: 사진을 몇 장 찍었는지는 나오지 않는다. ① a man ② Yes(부탁받았다) ③ in a building ⑤ Yes. 질문은 본문·통합본 T/F 문장을 의문문으로 바꾼 것.
items.source: L6 본문 1~2문단 · 통합본 L6 READING T/F 01~06

items.stem: <보기>의 (A)~(E)를 윗글에서 일어난 일의 순서로 바르게 배열한 것은?

box.title: < 보 기 >
lines: (A) Dr. Schofield hoped the world would learn about the event.
(B) On February 28, 1919, a man came to Dr. Schofield's house.
(C) He began to take pictures.
(D) The man asked Dr. Schofield to take pictures of an important event.
(E) Dr. Schofield was hiding in a building and saw a large group of people gathering outside.

items.explain: 2월 28일 남자가 찾아옴 → 부탁 → 3월 1일 건물에 숨어 사람들이 모이는 것을 봄 → 사진을 찍기 시작 → 세계가 알게 되기를 바람. 보기는 본문·통합본 T/F 문장 그대로.
items.source: L6 본문 1~2문단 · 통합본 L6 READING T/F 01·03·06

lines: Modern street art comes in many different forms, and it makes cities colorful and lively. Today, we are going to see some well-known street artworks in London. The place that we are going to visit is Shoreditch. ⓐ[Poor / Rich] workers used to live in this area, but now it is one of the hippest areas in London. We can find so many great pieces of street art here. (A) Do you see the painting over there? (B) He is famous for using only ⓑ[lines / colors] and dots in his paintings of human bodies. (C) According to STIK, the three figures represent the past, present, and future of Shoreditch. (D) Which figure represents which? Well, look ⓒ[closely / quickly] at the eyes of the three figures. (E) They are just dots, but they will give you a clue.

items.stem: 윗글의 흐름상 다음 문장이 들어갈 가장 적절한 곳은?
items.box: It is by the artist STIK.
items.explain: It = the painting over there. 그림을 가리킨 뒤 작가가 STIK임을 밝히고, 그다음 He(STIK)를 설명한다.

items.stem: 윗글의 흐름상 ⓐ~ⓒ에 들어갈 단어로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
items.explain: but now it is one of the hippest areas → 예전엔 Poor workers / 선(lines)과 점(dots)만 사용 / 단서를 찾으려면 자세히(closely) 본다.

items.stem: 다음 중 밑줄 친 that의 쓰임이 다른 하나는?
choices: The place <u>that</u> we are going to visit is Shoreditch.
The song <u>that</u> I listened to yesterday was really peaceful.
The car <u>that</u> Ally drives is brand-new.
He is so young <u>that</u> he can't ride the roller coaster.
The girl <u>that</u> I met in the park is Mina.
items.explain: ④는 so ~ that 구문의 접속사 that. 나머지는 목적격 관계대명사 that.
items.source: L5 본문 1문단 · 학습지 p.6 Practice A-4 · 통합본 L5·L6 GRAMMAR

lines: An Interview with Dr. Schofield
Interviewer: Dr. Schofield, I hear you have a Korean name. Can you tell me about it?
Dr. Schofield: It's Seok Hopil. (A) <u>I love it because it sounds similar to my English name.</u> Also, it has a good meaning.
Interviewer: I'd like to know why you helped the Korean independence movement.
Dr. Schofield: Well, I believe every country has the right to be independent.
Interviewer: What did you do after you returned to Korea in 1958?
Dr. Schofield: I worked hard to help Koreans, especially poor students.

items.stem: 윗글의 맥락상 밑줄 친 (A)에서 추론할 수 있는 Dr. Schofield의 심경으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: pleased
bored
scared
worried
disappointed
items.explain: 자신의 한국 이름을 사랑한다고 말하므로 pleased(기쁜).

items.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Seok Hopil was Frank W. Schofield's Korean name.
His English name was Frank W. Schofield, but he loved his Korean name.
Dr. Schofield supported the Korean independence movement because he believed every country should be independent.
Dr. Schofield came back to Korea in 1920 because the Korean government invited him.
For the rest of his life, he worked hard to help Koreans, especially poor students.
items.explain: 한국 정부의 초청으로 돌아온 해는 1958년(What did you do after you returned to Korea in 1958?). 나머지는 본문·통합본 T/F 문장 그대로.
items.source: L6 After You Read · 통합본 L6 READING T/F 07·12·18

lines: We are now in Finsbury Park to see a painting by Banksy, an internationally famous street artist. Banksy's artworks often carry <u>social</u> messages, and the green tree you see over there is a good example. As you can see, he created a green tree by spraying green paint on a wall behind a leafless tree. Next to the tree, there is a person who is holding a sprayer. What message does Banksy want to give us through this painting? In many people's opinion, he is telling us that nature is having a hard time. They think he wants us to take better care of it.

items.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 social의 영영풀이로 옳은 것은?
choices: belonging or relating to one particular person
relating to human society and its organization
of the present or recent times
following the latest fashions in music and clothes
full of life and energy
items.explain: social(사회의): 인간 사회와 그 조직과 관련된. ① personal ③ modern ④ hip ⑤ lively.

items.stem: 윗글을 읽고 Banksy의 그림에 대해 바르게 이해한 학생은?
choices: S 1: "Banksy is a street artist who is only famous in London."
S 2: "Banksy's artworks usually include social messages."
S 3: "The tree in Banksy's artwork actually has real leaves."
S 4: "The person next to the tree is holding a camera."
S 5: "Banksy's artwork carries only personal messages."
items.explain: ② Banksy's artworks often carry social messages. ① internationally famous ③ a leafless tree(잎이 없는 나무 뒤 벽에 그림) ④ holding a sprayer ⑤ social messages. 학생 발화는 통합본 L5 본문 T/F·일치 문장 그대로.
items.source: L5 본문 2문단 · 통합본 L5 READING T/F 09~13·일치 ⑤

items.stem: 다음 문장들의 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 단어는?
items.box:
○ Could you take pictures _____ the event and share them with the world?
○ In 1958, he returned to Korea at the invitation _____ the Korean government and never left again.
choices: of
to
in
for
with
items.explain: take a picture of(~의 사진을 찍다), at the invitation of(~의 초대로).

items.stem: 다음 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것은?
choices: I was so hungry that I ate the whole cake.
It was so cold that we couldn't go on a picnic.
It was raining so heavily that we had to stay home.
The room is dark so that I can't see anything.
They talked so fast that I couldn't understand them.
items.explain: ‘너무 어두워서 볼 수 없다’는 so + 형용사 + that: The room is so dark that I can't see anything.

lines: Kim Mandeok was born in Jeju-do in 1739. She was a successful businesswoman. In 1795, she saw many people dying from hunger. So, she bought rice with all her money and gave it away to poor people. Her love for others was so selfless that many people respected her. From her life, I learned that selfless love for others can make a big difference.

items.stem: 윗글의 글쓴이가 Kim Mandeok의 삶에서 배운 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Everyone has the right to learn.
Selfless love for others can make a big difference.
Modern street art makes cities colorful and lively.
People are working together to create the artworks.
She did a lot of volunteer work, especially for children.
items.explain: From her life, I learned that selfless love for others can make a big difference. ① L6 다의어 예문 ③ L5 본문 ④ L5 Culture Project ⑤ L6 대화문(Audrey Hepburn) 문장.

items.stem: 윗글을 다음과 같이 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓒ에 들어갈 말로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
items.box: She was a ⓐ___ businesswoman. In 1795, she saw many people dying from hunger. So, she bought ⓑ___ with all her money and gave it away to poor people. Her love for others was so selfless that many people ⓒ___ her.
items.explain: a successful businesswoman / bought rice / many people respected her. 본문 문장 그대로에 빈칸을 두었다.

lines: Do you know Seok Hopil? His English name was Frank W. Schofield, but he loved his Korean name. It sounded similar to his real name, and it also had a good meaning.

Dr. Schofield was a Canadian doctor, and he first came to Korea in 1916 to teach medicine. He wanted to teach in Korean, so he began to learn Korean right away. (가) <u>그는 매우 열심히 공부해서 몇 년 만에 한국어로 가르칠 수 있게 되었다.</u> He believed that every country has the right to be independent, so he helped the Korean independence movement.

items.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Dr. Schofield came to Korea in 1916 to teach mathematics.
Dr. Schofield could teach in Korean after only a few months.
Dr. Schofield was a doctor from Canada.
Seok Hopil was Frank W. Schofield's English name.
Dr. Schofield began to learn Korean because he wanted to teach in English.
items.explain: ① medicine ② a few years ④ Korean name ⑤ to teach in Korean. 선지는 통합본 L6 본문 T/F 문장 그대로(④⑤는 한 단어만 바꿈).
items.source: L6 본문 3~4문단 · 통합본 L6 READING T/F 07~11

items.stem: 윗글을 읽고 Dr. Schofield에 대해 바르게 이해한 학생은?
choices: S 1: "He first came to Korea in 1916 to learn medicine."
S 2: "He wanted to teach in English, so he began to learn Korean right away."
S 3: "He believed that every country has the right to be independent, so he helped the Korean independence movement."
S 4: "He studied so hard that he was able to teach in Korean after only a few months."
S 5: "His English name was Frank W. Schofield, but he hated his Korean name."
items.explain: ③ 본문 문장 그대로. ① to teach medicine ② to teach in Korean ④ a few years ⑤ loved his Korean name — 본문 문장에서 한 단어씩 바꾼 것.

items.stem: 윗글의 밑줄 친 우리말 (가)를 <조건>에 맞춰 바르게 영작하시오.
condition: 다음 단어를 반드시 사용할 것 (※ 단, 필요시 단어의 형태를 변형할 것): study, so, that, be able to, only a few years
items.answer: He studied so hard that he was able to teach in Korean after only a few years.
items.explain: so + 부사(hard) + that + 주어 + 동사: 매우 ~해서 …하다. 15단어.
items.source: L6 본문 4문단 · 통합본 L6 GRAMMAR so ~ that

items.stem: 다음 문장들의 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓒ에 들어갈 단어가 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
items.box:
○ He is famous ⓐ___ using only lines and dots in his paintings of human bodies.
○ I'm really interested ⓑ___ science. Can you recommend a science magazine for me?
○ Could you take pictures of the event and share them ⓒ___ the world?
items.explain: be famous for(~로 유명하다), be interested in(~에 관심이 있다), share A with B(A를 B와 공유하다).
items.source: L5 본문 1문단 · L6 Watch and Talk A-4 · L6 본문 1문단

items.stem: 다음 대화에서 A, B의 관계로 가장 적절한 것은?
items.box:
A: Excuse me. I'm going to the National Art Museum. What's the best way to get there?
B: You can walk. Go straight for about 500 meters and turn left. It'll be on your right.
A: I see. How long will it take?
B: Only about 15 minutes.
A: Really? Thanks.
items.explain: 길을 묻는 관광객(tourist)과 길을 알려 주는 행인(passerby).

lines: G: Liam, can you please help me? I need to find some books for my homework.
B: What kinds of books are you looking for, Somi?
G: I'm looking for books on famous people who helped others. I need to write an essay.
B: Who do you want to write about?
G: I was thinking about Dr. Schweitzer, but <u>나에게 다른 사람을 추천해 줄 수 있어?</u>
B: What about Audrey Hepburn?
G: I know she was a famous actor, but what did she do to help others?
B: She did a lot of volunteer work, especially for children.
G: Really? Then, I can write about her. Thank you!

items.stem: 다음은 Somi가 대화 후에 적은 메모이다. 위 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

box.title: My Essay Plan
lines: ① I need to find some books for my homework.
② I'm looking for books on famous people who helped others.
③ I was thinking about Dr. Schweitzer.
④ Audrey Hepburn was a famous singer that helped others.
⑤ She did a lot of volunteer work, especially for children.

choices: ①
②
③
④
⑤
items.explain: I know she was a famous actor(배우). 메모 문장은 대화문·통합본 L6 대화 일치 문장 그대로. 그림·표 대신 메모 글로 물었다.
items.source: L6 Watch and Talk C · 통합본 L6 DIALOGUES 일치 ④

items.stem: 위 대화의 밑줄 친 우리말을 <조건>에 맞춰 바르게 영작하시오.
condition: 다음 단어를 반드시 사용할 것: can, recommend, someone else
items.answer: can you recommend someone else for me?
items.explain: 추천을 부탁하는 표현 Can you recommend ~ for me? 7단어.

items.stem: 다음 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것은?
choices: I used to skip breakfast, but now I eat breakfast every day.
I didn't use to like coffee, but now I drink two cups every day.
Did this place use to be a bookstore a long time ago?
There used to be a large park here before the new shopping mall was built.
He isn't used to speak in front of many people yet.
items.explain: ‘~에 익숙하다’는 be used to + -ing: isn't used to speaking. 나머지는 used to(과거의 습관·상태)의 평서·부정·의문문.

items.stem: 다음 중 우리말 영작이 바르지 않은 것은?
choices:
나는 주말마다 테니스를 치곤 했다.
→ I used to play tennis every weekend.

정원에는 사과나무가 많이 있었다. (지금은 없음)
→ There used to be many apple trees in the garden.

나는 브로콜리를 좋아하지 않았었지만, 지금은 즐겨 먹는다.
→ I didn't use to like broccoli, but I enjoy it now.

너는 어렸을 때 축구를 하곤 했니?
→ Did you used to play soccer when you were young?

이 칼은 야채를 자르는 데 사용된다.
→ This knife is used to cut vegetables.
items.explain: used to의 의문문은 Did + 주어 + use to + 동사원형: Did you use to play ~?

items.stem: 다음 중 어법상 옳은 것은?
choices: Picasso is the painter which I like the most.
I love the cookies whom my mom made.
This is the museum which I want to visit in London.
The girl which I met in the park is Mina.
This is the house in that I lived.
items.explain: ① 사람 선행사 → whom/that ② 사물 선행사 → which/that ④ 사람 → whom/that ⑤ 전치사 뒤에는 that 불가 → in which(학습지 p.5 표). ③ 사물 선행사 + which 옳다.
items.source: 통합본 L5 GRAMMAR 목적격 관계대명사 연습 01~07 · 학습지 p.5

items.stem: 다음 대화의 밑줄 친 Dr. Schofield의 우리말을 <조건>에 맞춰 바르게 영작하시오.
items.box:
Interviewer: I'd like to know why you helped the Korean independence movement.
Dr. Schofield: Well, <u>저는 모든 나라는 독립할 권리가 있다고 믿어요.</u>
condition: 다음 단어를 반드시 사용할 것: believe, every country, the right, independent
items.answer: I believe every country has the right to be independent.
items.explain: believe (that) + 절, the right to + 동사원형(~할 권리). 10단어.

items.stem: <보기>와 같이 주어진 두 문장을 한 문장으로 완성하시오.

box.title: < 보 기 >
lines: The book was very interesting. + I read it yesterday.
⇨ The book which I read yesterday was very interesting.
The story was funny. + You talked about it.

items.answer: The story which[that] you talked about was funny.
items.explain: 전치사 about의 목적어 it을 대신하는 목적격 관계대명사 which/that. (about which you talked도 가능)
